newsitem.title: USA: US West Coast lt. crude stays firm, ANS diffs flat.
newsitem.headline: US West Coast lt. crude stays firm, ANS diffs flat.

text.p: U.S. West Coast light crudes added modestly to yesterday's gains early Thursday, tracking West Texas Intermediate (WTI) amid quiet discussion, traders said.
Most spot crude traders attended an industry function Thursday, leaving discounts unchanged after yesterday's sale of Alaska North Slope grade at $0.80 cents under WTI.
No deals were heard done in heavy crudes or light Line 63 grades.
ANS crude ranged $19.90/20.10 a barrel, up 20 cents from Wednesday.

West Coast refiners last week upped their refining operations, according to API. Operating capacity stood 83.8 percent, a 4.3 percent-point increase, as Exxon and Mobil brought units back from maintenance shutdowns, traders and companies said..
Line 63 stood unchanged at postings plus $0.95 - $1.05.
Kern River, a representative heavy grade, stood $14.25/14.35 a barrel, unchanged from Wednesday.
